metadata:

name: decade-and-recency-screen
description: MAP screen on conservative_updating_inflated_size base — decade-aligned interval priors are null; recency graft +0.5 nats
metadata:

- Interval prior boost for decade-aligned intervals (1-10, 11-20, ... and also the 50-59 "tens digit" style): boost ~0.1-0.8, gain 0.0 nats, p_yes RMSE 0.0002. The critique's decade_boundary_effect cannot be closed via interval priors. Do not retry.

**Why:** saves re-screening dead ideas.

name: decade-boundary-range-extent
description: decade_partitioned_number_line (iter_3 cand_1) — decade crossings add perceived range extent; MAP gain tiny
metadata:
  type: project
---
On 2026-10-21 (experiment3, iter_3, candidate_1), the critique flagged decade_boundary_effect: same-decade near targets get more yeses than the model predicts (q=0.21, not FDR-significant). The candidate decade_partitioned_number_line responds with serial_position_ends_inflated_size plus one change: a range's perceived size becomes width + decade_distance × (decade boundaries crossed), with a HalfNormal(5) prior on decade_distance. Interval groups get an extra crossing key, which raises them from about 450 to 748 per set.

At MAP, decade_distance came out at about 0.96. The log-likelihood was -3188.7, against -3189.1 for the best model, a gain of only 0.4 nats. p_yes RMSE against the best model on the data trials was 0.0032.

**Why:** the decade effect is weak in these data, and a range-prior version (round_landmark_interval_prior) was already pruned.
**How to apply:** do not expect decade or landmark range tweaks to win. See [[map-screening-refinements]].

Convergence repair (2026-10-21, iter_3 candidate_1_repair_1): the original failed R-hat 1.051 / ESS 76. Swapping HalfNormal priors for LogNormal (decade_distance LogNormal(0,0.5); size_inflation LogNormal(log 1.5,0.75)) fixed it. A 4-chain warm-start benchmark (200/250, ta 0.95) gave max R-hat 1.01, min ESS 424 (size_inflation), 0 divergences, 15 steps per iteration, 1230 s on load ~58. Posterior decade_distance 1.06 ± 0.50 (prior-dominated).
**How to apply:** for warm-start NUTS, use LogNormal rather than HalfNormal on positive scale params with posterior mass near 0. The dense Hessian metric fits poorly when the log-space posterior has a long tail.

name: incumbent-saturation-screens
description: iter_3 MAP screens on serial_position_ends_inflated_size — what was null, and that freeing the rule-weight prior gained
metadata:
  type: project
---
Experiment3 iter_3 candidate_4 (2026-10-21). MAP screens on the incumbent serial_position_ends_inflated_size (its MAP log-lik is -3189.1):
- Decade-aligned range prior boost (decade_boundary critique, q=0.21). Null under both decade definitions (tens digit, and (x-1)//10): the boost goes to about 0 and log-lik does not change.
- Uniform check lapse for arithmetic rules: -0.3 nats.
- Per-cell excess deviance is 661 over 1312 cells, about the chi-square expectation, so the model is at the noise ceiling with only 5 responses per cell.
- Replacing Dirichlet(2) rule_weights with spread*ZeroSumNormal + a HalfNormal(1.5) spread gained +3.4 nats at MAP (spread about 4.4, p_yes RMSE 0.0115). The Dirichlet(2) prior over-shrinks the rule weights. Submitted as pooled_rule_familiarity_spread.

**Why:** avoids re-screening dead ideas; the rule-weight prior is the live lever.
**How to apply:** see [[map-screening-refinements]]; scripts are in iter_3/candidate_4/scratch (mapfit.py, resid.py, bench.py).

Repair (iter_3 candidate_4_repair_1, final attempt): pooled_rule_familiarity_spread timed out at target_accept 0.99, a HalfNormal-spread funnel. The fix, uneven_rule_familiarity_ends:
- Fixed spread 3.0 × ZeroSumNormal z, with z projected orthogonal to the centred log-size direction so it cannot trade off with size_exponent.
- MAP log-lik -3186.4, which is +2.7 nats; p_yes RMSE vs the incumbent 0.0089.
- First benchmark: 31 steps per iteration, 0 divergences, but size_inflation (HalfNormal(10)) had ESS 8.
- Switching size_inflation to LogNormal(log 1.5, 0.75) raised its ESS to 119, with a minimum of 79 over 250 draws, in 435 s.
**How to apply:** on this base, put a LogNormal prior on size_inflation, never HalfNormal; it is the slowest-mixing parameter.

name: map-screening-refinements
description: Fast MAP screen (~1 min) to compare refinements of the inflated_size_familiar_rule_prior incumbent before the slow check
metadata:
  type: project
---
On 2026-10-21 (experiment3, iter_2, candidate_4), pm.find_MAP on the model_loop responses took about 45 s for incumbent variants. The incumbent's MAP log-likelihood was -3190.1. Its posterior means (log_gain 0.21, size_inflation 1.3, anchor_weight 0.93, size_exponent 0.74) differ from the design fit cache in experiment3/design/_fit_cache.

One-parameter tweaks each gained at most about 1 nat:
- interval width-power prior
- anchoring on the last example
- belief floor
- set-size-dependent gain
- redundancy exponent

Replacing the 42 per-rule Dirichlet weights with 8 equal-within-family weights lost about 1260 nats, so individual rule weights are essential.

Sampling examples without replacement (no_repeat_example_sampling) gained 1.45 nats with no new parameter.

Residuals left after MAP: generalization to unseen members of powers of 2 and multiples of 7 is overpredicted.

**Why:** cheap screening avoids spending 12-minute checks on dead ideas.
**How to apply:** script pattern is at /tmp/c4/mapfit.py (may be gone); rebuild it with pm.set_data(prepare_observed(rows)) and find_MAP, and compare p_yes RMSE against the incumbent (>0.002 is needed for novelty). See [[volatile-model-speed]].

Pitfall: read p_yes from the find_MAP result dict (mp["p_yes"]). compile_fn on a Deterministic with value-var inputs silently samples the RVs. no_repeat_example_sampling at MAP: loglik -3188.7 vs -3190.1, p_yes RMSE vs incumbent 0.0041.

name: order-effects-null
description: Order/sequential mechanisms screened at MAP in experiment3 iter_3 — data strongly favour order-blind accumulation
metadata:
  type: project
---
2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_3 candidate_0 (exploratory slot, order brief), on the inflated_size_familiar_rule_prior base (MAP loglik -3190.1):
- Surprise-weighted evidence (each later example's weight = exp(-eta * log(100 * predictive prob)), soft-capped): MAP eta = -0.008. The profile is sharp: eta = -0.5 costs 44 nats, +0.5 costs 146. Submitted as surprise_weighted_sequential_evidence. Predictions are sensitive to eta (±0.05 gives RMSE 0.02), so novelty should be OK.
- First example alone sets the rule-vs-range family belief, with later examples counting by a fraction lambda at the family level: MAP lambda = 0.97, loglik -3190.5. Null.
**Why:** order/position ideas keep collapsing to the order-blind model. Only one set ("8,16"/"16,8") appears in two orders.
**How to apply:** for order briefs, expect the null; prefer mechanisms whose predictions move strongly with the parameter (to pass novelty) or accept a falsification result. Pitfall: evaluate p_yes at fixed values with pm.do(model, {all free RVs: values})["p_yes"].eval(). See [[map-screening-refinements]], [[volatile-model-speed]].

name: size-inflation-softplus
description: Convergence fix for incumbent-family models — size_inflation is the worst-mixing param; softplus(Normal) beats HalfNormal/LogNormal
metadata:
  type: project
---
2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_3 candidate_2_repair_1 (adaptive_breadth_criterion): admission rejected for R-hat 1.054 / ESS 67. A 2-chain warm-start bench (250/250) showed size_inflation was the bottleneck (posterior ~2.3 ± 1.0, roughly symmetric on the linear scale, so skewed in log space). Bulk ESS: HalfNormal(10) 181, LogNormal(log 3, 0.75) 223, softplus(Normal(2.5, 1.5)) 734. After the change the min ESS over all params was 584, with no divergences.
Also centre/scale any set-level covariate (log breadth mean 0.71, sd 0.2 at MAP) so its slope does not trade off with bias.
**Why:** the warm-start fixed dense mass matrix assumes Gaussian geometry; skewed params mix badly.
**How to apply:** for convergence rejections on this base, bench with /tmp/c2r/bench.py (PYTHONPATH=. needed) and reparameterise size_inflation via softplus. See [[volatile-model-speed]], [[slow-fit-diagnosis]], [[adaptive-breadth-criterion]].

name: slow-fit-diagnosis
description: How to diagnose a too-slow candidate fit (Hessian at mode, leapfrog steps/iter) and what fixed schema_grammar_rule_prior
metadata:
  type: project
---
On 2026-10-21 (experiment3 iter_2 candidate_2_repair_1), schema_grammar_rule_prior timed out. At its mode the 8 Dirichlet schema weights, p_mix and size_exponent were constrained only by their priors: Hessian eigenvalues of about 2 matched the Dirichlet(2) prior. The fit was degenerate (gain about 0.14, rule evidence weight about 4, log-lik -4454 against the incumbent's -3190).

The repair dropped the schema weights and size_exponent (a fixed uniform grammar prior), giving rule_grammar_uniform_prior. That brought the fit to about 15 leapfrog steps per iteration (incumbent about 28), with no divergences.

A centre-weighted range sampling idea (shape (4u(1-u))^peak) was also tried: its MAP peak was about 0.06 and it gained only 0.3 nats, so it is a near-duplicate of the incumbent. Do not retry it.

**Why:** if parameters are pinned only by their priors, or the mode is degenerate, NUTS takes long trajectories.
**How to apply:**
- To diagnose, run L-BFGS on step._logp_dlogp_func, then look at the Hessian eigenvalues and the correlation matrix.
- To time a fit, call src.models.pymc_inference._warm_start_sample with tune=draws=40 and chains=1, then read sample_stats n_steps.

See [[volatile-model-speed]] and [[map-screening-refinements]].

name: volatile-model-speed
description: How to keep volatile-changepoint concept models fast enough for the 30-min admission fit
metadata:
  type: project
---
Volatile changepoint models (sequential update over 42 rules + interval groups) are near the 30-min admission limit; the machine is heavily loaded (1 CPU visible, load ~25).
Tricks that helped (2026-10-21, experiment3 candidate_5_repair_1): bucket sets by example count so each bucket runs only its own updates; drop the noise log-lik constant (it cancels on normalisation); avoid adding parameters that trade off (e.g. range inflation + range tempering).
**Why:** volatile_split_rule_range_inflation was rejected as too slow. Its repair took depth ~5 (31 steps), about 6 min per chain at 200 tune / 250 draws.
**How to apply:** benchmark with src.models.pymc_inference._warm_start_sample at target_accept 0.99 before finishing.

Timing reference (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_1 candidate_1): the non-volatile incumbent inflated_size_familiar_rule_prior plus one parameter took ~14 min wall time for check_candidate (100 tune / 100 draws, 1 chain), compile included, on the loaded machine. Use background runs.

Non-volatile models built on inflated_size_familiar_rule_prior are slow too: the check_candidate smoke fit (100 tune + 100 draws, 1 chain) took ~340 s per run on 2026-10-21 (load ~9), and the full check takes ~12 min. So run the check in the background with a long timeout and redirect its output to a file, not `| tail`. inferred_stray_example_rate on that base was dropped as too slow in a fold fit.

Repair strategy (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_1 candidate_5_repair_1, final attempt): volatile_final_digit_union_concepts (volatile base + 375 digit-union concepts) timed out at 30 min. The repair moved the same union mechanism onto the non-volatile inflated_concept_size_principle base, as final_digit_union_inflated_size, with unions collapsed into at most 30 groups per set by (arity, examples inside, anchor inside). On a final repair, prefer a non-volatile base.

Note on novelty (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_1 candidate_3): splitting the incumbent's size inflation into separate rule and range inflations was rejected as a near-duplicate (p_yes RMSE 0.0013 < 0.002). The data do not separate those two inflations, so tweaks of that kind do not count as new. Final-digit unions, rule-check failures and surface-numeral fallback were all taken by other slots the same round. trial_index cannot be separated from stimulus, because each (set, target) cell sits at a single trial index.

Exploratory idea used (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_2 candidate_0): set_size_triggered_rule_search. It is the incumbent with the prior share of rules (p_mix) given a logit slope over set size, centred at 3 examples. It adds one parameter, so the cost stays close to the incumbent's.

Idea log (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_2 candidate_2): schema_grammar_rule_prior. It replaces the incumbent's 42 Dirichlet rule weights with 8 schema weights split equally within each schema, times size**exponent. A simpler, faster, high-variance test of whether rule-specific familiarity matters.

Refinement used (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_2 candidate_3): serial_position_ends_inflated_size. It is the incumbent plus a last-example evidence multiplier (recency_weight), applied only to sets of 2+, with interval groups also split by whether the last example is inside. Data note: only one set ("8,16" vs "16,8") appears in two orders, so order effects show up mainly as position-within-set weighting. Pitfall: when splicing the incumbent source, split on the module docstring only (src.split(DOCQUOTE+"\n", 1)[1]). concept_sets() has its own docstring; maxsplit 2 silently drops code and gives "forbidden import: <unparseable source>" (hit again iter_3 candidate_5).

Timing (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_2 candidate_5): conservative_updating_inflated_size (the conservative linear-pool update on the volatile_changepoint_inflated_size code base) passed check_candidate. Sampling took 296 s and the whole check about 14 min wall time.

Cell-level trick (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_2 candidate_1_repair_1): the model_loop data have 6750 trials but only 1312 distinct (set, target) cells and 180 sets. Compute interval membership sums and p over cells, then set p_yes = p_cell[row_cell]. This cuts the dominant (trials x ~446 groups) operations about 5x. queried_target_self_evidence took 697 s per smoke fit before this change and was rejected as too slow.

Per-cell trick (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_2 candidate_0_repair_1): the incumbent-family code builds `group_in_concept` as (trials x groups), 6750 rows. Computing predictions per distinct (set, target) cell instead (1312 cells: `cell_set`, `cell_group_share`, `cell_rule_in`, then `[row_cell]` to trials) cut the logp+grad time from 0.054 s to 0.018 s with identical logp. Apply it to any model copied from inflated_size_familiar_rule_prior. Note that 180 distinct sets exist; a naive `cut -d,` count is wrong because of the quoted commas.

Speed fix (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_2): all six iter_2 candidates timed out at 30 min (load was ~38). Most were incumbent + 1 parameter. In the candidate_4_repair_1 rewrite, p_yes was computed per distinct (set, target) cell, 1312 cells versus 6750 trials, then indexed by row_cell. Also, mask/remaining-size arrays were precomputed instead of using pt.switch loops. Together these cut the gradient eval to ~1/3 of the incumbent's. Apply this cell trick to any model on this base.

Speed fix for the non-volatile base (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_2 candidate_3_repair_1): the data have only 1312 distinct (set, target) cells across 6750 trials, and at most 39 targets are asked per set. Replace the per-trial `group_in_concept` (trials x groups) with share tensors padded to the asked targets, (sets, groups, 39) and (sets, rules, 39). Compute `pt.batched_dot(posterior, share)` once per set, then index trials by row_cell. This brought logp+grad from 53 ms to 12 ms with identical MAP. Elementwise multiply-and-sum was slower than batched_dot, and per-cell gathers were also slower. no_repeat_example_sampling and serial_position_ends_inflated_size both timed out at target_accept 0.99 on the old layout. Profile pattern: /tmp/c3r/prof.py (may be gone).
Result: check_candidate passed with OK. The smoke fit sampled in ~125 s per run, versus ~340 s before; whole check ~10 min.

Timeout repair (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_2 candidate_5_repair_1): conservative_updating_inflated_size timed out at admission even though its smoke check had passed. A warm-start benchmark at target_accept 0.99 (150/150 draws) showed the same depth as the incumbent (~31 steps). The fix had two parts:
- Better-identified parameters: one shared evidence weight, since the rule and range weights were nearly equal, and a LogNormal(log 3, 0.75) prior on size_inflation instead of HalfNormal.
- Cheaper gradients: sort sets by size, largest first, and run each update step k only on log_post[:n_active[k]] with pt.set_subtensor. This cut one gradient from 0.067 s to 0.047 s; the incumbent's is ~0.053 s.

The benchmark script is at /tmp/c5r/bench.py (it may be gone). It must run from the repo cwd and not with -I, or pyprojroot fails.
Result: the per-cell set_size_triggered_rule_search ran warm-start NUTS at target_accept 0.99 (200 tune / 250 draws, 1 chain) in 278 s, tree depth 5, 0 divergences. Its check_candidate smoke fit took 121 s, against about 340 s before. The posterior slope was 0.07 ± 0.19, near zero, so it is a novelty risk.

- Decade-aligned range prior boost (decade_boundary critique, q=0.21). Null under both decade definitions (tens digit, and (x-1)//10): the boost goes to about 0 and log-lik does not change.
- Uniform check lapse for arithmetic rules: -0.3 nats.
- Per-cell excess deviance is 661 over 1312 cells, about the chi-square expectation, so the model is at the noise ceiling with only 5 responses per cell.

**How to apply:** see [[map-screening-refinements]]; scripts are in iter_3/candidate_4/scratch (mapfit.py, resid.py, bench.py).

Repair (iter_3 candidate_4_repair_1, final attempt): pooled_rule_familiarity_spread timed out at target_accept 0.99, a HalfNormal-spread funnel. The fix, uneven_rule_familiarity_ends:
- Fixed spread 3.0 × ZeroSumNormal z, with z projected orthogonal to the centred log-size direction so it cannot trade off with size_exponent.
- MAP log-lik -3186.4, which is +2.7 nats; p_yes RMSE vs the incumbent 0.0089.
- First benchmark: 31 steps per iteration, 0 divergences, but size_inflation (HalfNormal(10)) had ESS 8.
- Switching size_inflation to LogNormal(log 1.5, 0.75) raised its ESS to 119, with a minimum of 79 over 250 draws, in 435 s.
**How to apply:** on this base, put a LogNormal prior on size_inflation, never HalfNormal; it is the slowest-mixing parameter.

name: map-screening-refinements
description: Fast MAP screen (~1 min) to compare refinements of the inflated_size_familiar_rule_prior incumbent before the slow check
metadata:
  type: project
---
On 2026-10-21 (experiment3, iter_2, candidate_4), pm.find_MAP on the model_loop responses took about 45 s for incumbent variants. The incumbent's MAP log-likelihood was -3190.1. Its posterior means (log_gain 0.21, size_inflation 1.3, anchor_weight 0.93, size_exponent 0.74) differ from the design fit cache in experiment3/design/_fit_cache.

One-parameter tweaks each gained at most about 1 nat:
- interval width-power prior
- anchoring on the last example
- belief floor
- set-size-dependent gain
- redundancy exponent

Replacing the 42 per-rule Dirichlet weights with 8 equal-within-family weights lost about 1260 nats, so individual rule weights are essential.

Sampling examples without replacement (no_repeat_example_sampling) gained 1.45 nats with no new parameter.

Residuals left after MAP: generalization to unseen members of powers of 2 and multiples of 7 is overpredicted.

**Why:** cheap screening avoids spending 12-minute checks on dead ideas.
**How to apply:** script pattern is at /tmp/c4/mapfit.py (may be gone); rebuild it with pm.set_data(prepare_observed(rows)) and find_MAP, and compare p_yes RMSE against the incumbent (>0.002 is needed for novelty). See [[volatile-model-speed]].

Pitfall: read p_yes from the find_MAP result dict (mp["p_yes"]). compile_fn on a Deterministic with value-var inputs silently samples the RVs. no_repeat_example_sampling at MAP: loglik -3188.7 vs -3190.1, p_yes RMSE vs incumbent 0.0041.

Further nulls (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_3 candidate_3; serial_position_ends_inflated_size base, MAP loglik -3189.1):
- Decade categories as rule-like concepts with a prior share, using either the (x-1)//10 or the x//10 convention: share goes to about 0.005, gain 0.1 nats, RMSE vs incumbent 0.0014-0.0021. The critique's decade_boundary_effect (q=0.21) is not capturable this way.
- Inferred example-noise rate: estimate 0.106 (fixed value is 0.1), RMSE 0.0011, a null.
- Residual checks: parity and example-target calibration are fine. The incumbent is well calibrated; per-cell residuals look like noise (5 responses per cell).
- [Volatile model speed](volatile-model-speed.md) — keeping sequential concept models under the fit time limit; prefer non-volatile base on final repair
- [MAP screening](map-screening-refinements.md) — 1-min find_MAP screen for incumbent refinements; what gained/failed
- [Slow-fit diagnosis](slow-fit-diagnosis.md) — Hessian/steps-per-iter diagnosis; prior-only params cause timeouts; centre-weighted ranges = null
- [Adaptive breadth criterion](adaptive-breadth-criterion.md) — decision criterion tied to expected concept size; +2.2 nats MAP
- [Decade range extent](decade-boundary-range-extent.md) — decade-crossing range-size penalty gains ~0.4 nats at MAP; LogNormal priors fixed its R-hat failure

name: order-effects-null
description: Order/sequential mechanisms screened at MAP in experiment3 iter_3 — data strongly favour order-blind accumulation
metadata:
  type: project
---
2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_3 candidate_0 (exploratory slot, order brief), on the inflated_size_familiar_rule_prior base (MAP loglik -3190.1):
- Surprise-weighted evidence (each later example's weight = exp(-eta * log(100 * predictive prob)), soft-capped): MAP eta = -0.008. The profile is sharp: eta = -0.5 costs 44 nats, +0.5 costs 146. Submitted as surprise_weighted_sequential_evidence. Predictions are sensitive to eta (±0.05 gives RMSE 0.02), so novelty should be OK.
- First example alone sets the rule-vs-range family belief, with later examples counting by a fraction lambda at the family level: MAP lambda = 0.97, loglik -3190.5. Null.
**Why:** order/position ideas keep collapsing to the order-blind model. Only one set ("8,16"/"16,8") appears in two orders.
**How to apply:** for order briefs, expect the null; prefer mechanisms whose predictions move strongly with the parameter (to pass novelty) or accept a falsification result. Pitfall: evaluate p_yes at fixed values with pm.do(model, {all free RVs: values})["p_yes"].eval(). See [[map-screening-refinements]], [[volatile-model-speed]].
---
name: size-inflation-softplus
description: Convergence fix for incumbent-family models — size_inflation is the worst-mixing param; softplus(Normal) beats HalfNormal/LogNormal
metadata:
  type: project
---
2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_3 candidate_2_repair_1 (adaptive_breadth_criterion): admission rejected for R-hat 1.054 / ESS 67. A 2-chain warm-start bench (250/250) showed size_inflation was the bottleneck (posterior ~2.3 ± 1.0, roughly symmetric on the linear scale, so skewed in log space). Bulk ESS: HalfNormal(10) 181, LogNormal(log 3, 0.75) 223, softplus(Normal(2.5, 1.5)) 734. After the change the min ESS over all params was 584, with no divergences.
Also centre/scale any set-level covariate (log breadth mean 0.71, sd 0.2 at MAP) so its slope does not trade off with bias.
**Why:** the warm-start fixed dense mass matrix assumes Gaussian geometry; skewed params mix badly.
**How to apply:** for convergence rejections on this base, bench with /tmp/c2r/bench.py (PYTHONPATH=. needed) and reparameterise size_inflation via softplus. See [[volatile-model-speed]], [[slow-fit-diagnosis]], [[adaptive-breadth-criterion]].

name: slow-fit-diagnosis
description: How to diagnose a too-slow candidate fit (Hessian at mode, leapfrog steps/iter) and what fixed schema_grammar_rule_prior
metadata:
  type: project
---
On 2026-10-21 (experiment3 iter_2 candidate_2_repair_1), schema_grammar_rule_prior timed out. At its mode the 8 Dirichlet schema weights, p_mix and size_exponent were constrained only by their priors: Hessian eigenvalues of about 2 matched the Dirichlet(2) prior. The fit was degenerate (gain about 0.14, rule evidence weight about 4, log-lik -4454 against the incumbent's -3190).

The repair dropped the schema weights and size_exponent (a fixed uniform grammar prior), giving rule_grammar_uniform_prior. That brought the fit to about 15 leapfrog steps per iteration (incumbent about 28), with no divergences.

A centre-weighted range sampling idea (shape (4u(1-u))^peak) was also tried: its MAP peak was about 0.06 and it gained only 0.3 nats, so it is a near-duplicate of the incumbent. Do not retry it.

**Why:** if parameters are pinned only by their priors, or the mode is degenerate, NUTS takes long trajectories.
**How to apply:**
- To diagnose, run L-BFGS on step._logp_dlogp_func, then look at the Hessian eigenvalues and the correlation matrix.
- To time a fit, call src.models.pymc_inference._warm_start_sample with tune=draws=40 and chains=1, then read sample_stats n_steps.

See [[volatile-model-speed]] and [[map-screening-refinements]].

name: volatile-model-speed
description: How to keep volatile-changepoint concept models fast enough for the 30-min admission fit
metadata:
  type: project
---
Volatile changepoint models (sequential update over 42 rules + interval groups) are near the 30-min admission limit; the machine is heavily loaded (1 CPU visible, load ~25).
Tricks that helped (2026-10-21, experiment3 candidate_5_repair_1): bucket sets by example count so each bucket runs only its own updates; drop the noise log-lik constant (it cancels on normalisation); avoid adding parameters that trade off (e.g. range inflation + range tempering).
**Why:** volatile_split_rule_range_inflation was rejected as too slow. Its repair took depth ~5 (31 steps), about 6 min per chain at 200 tune / 250 draws.
**How to apply:** benchmark with src.models.pymc_inference._warm_start_sample at target_accept 0.99 before finishing.

Timing reference (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_1 candidate_1): the non-volatile incumbent inflated_size_familiar_rule_prior plus one parameter took ~14 min wall time for check_candidate (100 tune / 100 draws, 1 chain), compile included, on the loaded machine. Use background runs.

Non-volatile models built on inflated_size_familiar_rule_prior are slow too: the check_candidate smoke fit (100 tune + 100 draws, 1 chain) took ~340 s per run on 2026-10-21 (load ~9), and the full check takes ~12 min. So run the check in the background with a long timeout and redirect its output to a file, not `| tail`. inferred_stray_example_rate on that base was dropped as too slow in a fold fit.

Repair strategy (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_1 candidate_5_repair_1, final attempt): volatile_final_digit_union_concepts (volatile base + 375 digit-union concepts) timed out at 30 min. The repair moved the same union mechanism onto the non-volatile inflated_concept_size_principle base, as final_digit_union_inflated_size, with unions collapsed into at most 30 groups per set by (arity, examples inside, anchor inside). On a final repair, prefer a non-volatile base.

Note on novelty (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_1 candidate_3): splitting the incumbent's size inflation into separate rule and range inflations was rejected as a near-duplicate (p_yes RMSE 0.0013 < 0.002). The data do not separate those two inflations, so tweaks of that kind do not count as new. Final-digit unions, rule-check failures and surface-numeral fallback were all taken by other slots the same round. trial_index cannot be separated from stimulus, because each (set, target) cell sits at a single trial index.

Exploratory idea used (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_2 candidate_0): set_size_triggered_rule_search. It is the incumbent with the prior share of rules (p_mix) given a logit slope over set size, centred at 3 examples. It adds one parameter, so the cost stays close to the incumbent's.

Idea log (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_2 candidate_2): schema_grammar_rule_prior. It replaces the incumbent's 42 Dirichlet rule weights with 8 schema weights split equally within each schema, times size**exponent. A simpler, faster, high-variance test of whether rule-specific familiarity matters.

Refinement used (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_2 candidate_3): serial_position_ends_inflated_size. It is the incumbent plus a last-example evidence multiplier (recency_weight), applied only to sets of 2+, with interval groups also split by whether the last example is inside. Data note: only one set ("8,16" vs "16,8") appears in two orders, so order effects show up mainly as position-within-set weighting. Pitfall: when splicing the incumbent source, split on the module docstring only (src.split(DOCQUOTE+"\n", 1)[1]). concept_sets() has its own docstring; maxsplit 2 silently drops code and gives "forbidden import: <unparseable source>" (hit again iter_3 candidate_5).

Timing (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_2 candidate_5): conservative_updating_inflated_size (the conservative linear-pool update on the volatile_changepoint_inflated_size code base) passed check_candidate. Sampling took 296 s and the whole check about 14 min wall time.

Cell-level trick (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_2 candidate_1_repair_1): the model_loop data have 6750 trials but only 1312 distinct (set, target) cells and 180 sets. Compute interval membership sums and p over cells, then set p_yes = p_cell[row_cell]. This cuts the dominant (trials x ~446 groups) operations about 5x. queried_target_self_evidence took 697 s per smoke fit before this change and was rejected as too slow.

Per-cell trick (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_2 candidate_0_repair_1): the incumbent-family code builds `group_in_concept` as (trials x groups), 6750 rows. Computing predictions per distinct (set, target) cell instead (1312 cells: `cell_set`, `cell_group_share`, `cell_rule_in`, then `[row_cell]` to trials) cut the logp+grad time from 0.054 s to 0.018 s with identical logp. Apply it to any model copied from inflated_size_familiar_rule_prior. Note that 180 distinct sets exist; a naive `cut -d,` count is wrong because of the quoted commas.

Speed fix (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_2): all six iter_2 candidates timed out at 30 min (load was ~38). Most were incumbent + 1 parameter. In the candidate_4_repair_1 rewrite, p_yes was computed per distinct (set, target) cell, 1312 cells versus 6750 trials, then indexed by row_cell. Also, mask/remaining-size arrays were precomputed instead of using pt.switch loops. Together these cut the gradient eval to ~1/3 of the incumbent's. Apply this cell trick to any model on this base.

Speed fix for the non-volatile base (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_2 candidate_3_repair_1): the data have only 1312 distinct (set, target) cells across 6750 trials, and at most 39 targets are asked per set. Replace the per-trial `group_in_concept` (trials x groups) with share tensors padded to the asked targets, (sets, groups, 39) and (sets, rules, 39). Compute `pt.batched_dot(posterior, share)` once per set, then index trials by row_cell. This brought logp+grad from 53 ms to 12 ms with identical MAP. Elementwise multiply-and-sum was slower than batched_dot, and per-cell gathers were also slower. no_repeat_example_sampling and serial_position_ends_inflated_size both timed out at target_accept 0.99 on the old layout. Profile pattern: /tmp/c3r/prof.py (may be gone).
Result: check_candidate passed with OK. The smoke fit sampled in ~125 s per run, versus ~340 s before; whole check ~10 min.

Timeout repair (2026-10-21, experiment3 iter_2 candidate_5_repair_1): conservative_updating_inflated_size timed out at admission even though its smoke check had passed. A warm-start benchmark at target_accept 0.99 (150/150 draws) showed the same depth as the incumbent (~31 steps). The fix had two parts:
- Better-identified parameters: one shared evidence weight, since the rule and range weights were nearly equal, and a LogNormal(log 3, 0.75) prior on size_inflation instead of HalfNormal.
- Cheaper gradients: sort sets by size, largest first, and run each update step k only on log_post[:n_active[k]] with pt.set_subtensor. This cut one gradient from 0.067 s to 0.047 s; the incumbent's is ~0.053 s.

The benchmark script is at /tmp/c5r/bench.py (it may be gone). It must run from the repo cwd and not with -I, or pyprojroot fails.
Result: the per-cell set_size_triggered_rule_search ran warm-start NUTS at target_accept 0.99 (200 tune / 250 draws, 1 chain) in 278 s, tree depth 5, 0 divergences. Its check_candidate smoke fit took 121 s, against about 340 s before. The posterior slope was 0.07 ± 0.19, near zero, so it is a novelty risk.

"""Pooled rule familiarity on primacy-and-recency concept learning.

Refinement of serial_position_ends_inflated_size: people do the same Bayesian
concept learning over 42 rules and all intervals of 1..100, 10% noisy examples,
perceived concept sizes inflated by a constant, evidence tempered separately for
rules and ranges, the first and last examples weighted by their own inferred
multipliers, a decision gain and shifted criterion. The one change is to the
prior over rules: a rule's familiarity is its size-based plausibility (a power
of its size) times an idiosyncratic familiarity factor drawn from a wide
log-normal spread, instead of a Dirichlet(2) weight that pulls every rule's
weight toward the others. A few rules can therefore be strongly familiar and
many barely entertained, far more unevenly than the refined model allows.
"""


import numpy as np

I've written the candidate `best_explanation_target_judgment`. It ties the incumbent at MAP, and the admission check passed with `OK`: the 100+100-draw smoke fit took 267 s and gave a finite log-likelihood.

**The hypothesis.** People infer the concept as `uneven_rule_familiarity_ends` does. What changes is how they judge a target. They don't add up the belief of every concept that contains it. Instead, as in single-category reasoning, they compare the best explanation that includes the target with the best explanation overall, softened by an inferred sharpness β. β = 1 is ordinary Bayesian averaging; large β is a pure best-explanation comparison.

**Implementation.** Belief is `(Σ_{h∋t} w^β / Σ w^β)^(1/β)`. To keep β from trading off with the evidence weights, the rule share, size exponent and evidence weights are sampled as effective values that already include β. β then scales the fixed-spread rule familiarities and sets the 1/β power on belief. There is one new parameter (`log_beta`, Normal(0, 0.75)), and gradients run at the incumbent's speed (about 14 ms).

**MAP screen (incumbent at −3186.35):**

| Version | Result | p_yes RMSE vs incumbent |
|---|---|---|
| Submitted | β ≈ 1.3, log-lik −3187.7 | 0.0044 (above the 0.002 novelty cut) |
| β fixed at 5 | costs 14 nats | — |
| β fixed at 0.5 | costs 8 nats | — |

So the data favour judging targets with a slightly sharper focus than plain averaging. A version where β left the rule familiarities alone had an RMSE of only 0.0020, right at the novelty cut, so I didn't use it.

**Two ideas I screened and dropped:**
- **Gaussian magnitude clusters in place of crisp ranges:** 115 to 168 nats worse for every width I tried, which rules this representation out on these data.
- **Graded range edges:** fits no better than the incumbent, is a near-duplicate of it (RMSE 0.00196), and its gradients are 3.4× slower.

**Not yet checked:** the smoke check doesn't test convergence, novelty on the 512-stimulus pool, or the 30-minute admission limit. The MAP RMSE of 0.0044 on the data trials is the only evidence of novelty so far. I also didn't target the critique's singleton-rule discrepancy, since it doesn't survive the FDR correction (q = 0.30).

I saved these screen results to the memory notes.
